about: Made by crates/engine/src/plugins/vectors from the engine's own constants; the edge imports it. max_manifest_bytes is the manifest's canonical JSON without its signature; max_manifest_json_bytes and max_manifest_values are the manifest as written in the package, signature included, every JSON value counted once (keys not); max_publish_body_bytes is the .zeron-plugin file as uploaded. reserved_ids are the manifest rule's: ids Zeron itself won't run ('Zeron already uses that name', the manifests cases' id_error). site_ids are the store site's own pages beside /plugins/<id> and /templates/<id>, and those two names: a device runs a plugin with one (but 'templates', which is a reserved id too) and uses a template with one, but the store never lists it, of either kind (the listing rule id_reserved, which no reservation lifts). known_permissions are every permission a manifest may ask for: one not among them is the manifest's problem ('It asks for "x", which isn't a permission Zeron knows'), read on a device and at the store alike. The cases that hold both sides to these rules are in docs/plugin-package-vectors.json.

consent.about: A program's name is lowercased and loses one Windows extension (windows_extensions) before it's looked up. It can do anything you can unless it's in contained. It gives full control when it's in full_control, as it is or with its trailing digits and dots taken off (python3.12 → python). commands_anything is every program that can do anything you can and is neither full_control nor held_to_its_own_rules. A host is local when it's localhost, a private or loopback address, ends .localhost .local .internal .lan .home.arpa .intranet .corp, has one label, or ends in a number (decimal or 0x hex); network_local is every host but * that is local, network_named every host that names one host exactly (not * or *.…) and isn't local.

file_names.about: Of a plugin's files and a template's alike. A short name is a '~' directly followed by an ASCII digit, anywhere in a path (Windows opens ZERON-~1.JSO as zeron-plugin.json). unseen: the characters, as [first, last] code points, no path may hold (HFS+ leaves some out of a name it looks up). selectors are allowed (ordinary emoji names have them), and a path is compared without them: fold drops them before anything else it does, and the collision rule drops them before NFC too. At publish: a plugin's short name, and either kind's unseen character, is bad_package (field files, its path); a template's short name is protected_file (field files, its path). One problem a path: of a plugin, its short name before its unseen character; of a template, its unseen character, then that it's protected, then its short name, then what screenshots/ may hold. A device refuses a plugin's package with either, and a template's with an unseen character, as bad_file; a template's short name is left out and named. What's installed already loads as it did. The file_names cases hold both sides to it.

keyword_claims: A keyword (already lowercase letters, digits, dashes and single spaces) is refused (bad_listing, field keywords) when, its parts split at '-' and ' ' and each folded as mark_claims folds, a part or all its parts joined spells, whole, with mark_claims' lookalikes (interchangeable and pairs too): one of mark_claims.words; a word of mark_claims.languages whose folded form is ASCII (any description reading); No badge lifts it ('zeron' in a keyword is anyone's). The listing cases named 'keywords:' hold both sides to it.

listing_causes.about: A bad_listing problem on a name, a description or keywords carries cause, one of causes, and, where there is one, word, for an app that says it in its own words: the device's check and the edge's answer alike (the edge's refusal gives field, cause and word beside error and message, those of its first problem, and each of its problems the same). name: too_long; unseen_char; mark_glyph (its claim is one of mark_claims.glyphs) or else mark_word. description: too_long (over max_description_len), else not_one_line; unseen_char; mark_glyph or mark_word. keywords: too_many (more than max_keywords), else repeated (word: the first keyword given again); keyword_shape (word: the keyword, none when it isn't text); mark_word (word: the keyword). unseen_char's word is the first character unseen refuses, as U+ and its code point in at least four uppercase hex digits. mark_glyph's and mark_word's word in a name or description is where it says its claim, as written: of the runs of its words (each word a run of characters but White_Space, as long as it goes; a run from its first word's start to its last's end, as written; at most written_max_words words), the shortest that, read as a name is (mark_claims), claims the same claim, the earliest of those; then without its first character while it still does, then without its last while it still does; the claim itself when no run does. Every word is without control or format characters (General_Category Cc, Cf) and any other Default_Ignorable_Code_Point, and is at most max_word_chars characters (cut there). The listing cases' problems hold both sides to it.

mark_claims.about: A listing's name or description may not claim the store's mark (amendment 45; bad_listing on that field). One rule, the device's check and the edge alike (crates/engine/src/plugins/mark.rs). Fold: Unicode NFKC, then full lowercase (as JavaScript's toLowerCase), then NFKD with every nonspacing mark (General_Category Mn) dropped, then every Default_Ignorable_Code_Point (variation selectors among them) and every enclosing mark (General_Category Me) removed. It claims the mark when the folded text has any of glyphs anywhere; or any of words as a whole word, as written (no ASCII letter or digit right before or after it); or, as a whole word in the folded text or in it with its spaced runs read as words, any of words spelled letter by letter with: the letter itself or any of lookalikes[letter] (for each letter of interchangeable's pairs, those of both letters), or for a letter in pairs, its characters in order, each it or one of its own lookalikes. A spaced run: single characters, each with a separator or the text's edge on either side, apart by 1 to max_spacing separators (White_Space, U+FEFF, or General_Category P*), read as one word with the separators gone. lookalikes is generated from source (Unicode's confusables.txt, at version, whose file's sha256 is sha256): every single-character source whose prototype folds to one of the letters of words or an ASCII letter of a languages word as mark_text folds it, kept both folded and as written unless either is an ASCII letter, plus the Latin small capitals, the boxed emoji letters (NEGATIVE CIRCLED and NEGATIVE SQUARED LATIN CAPITAL LETTERs, REGIONAL INDICATOR SYMBOL LETTERs) and the digit 3 for e. Then, in the store's other languages: each of languages[lang].words, in either reading, spelled letter by letter as the words are (each letter itself or one of its lookalikes; a letter that is itself one of lookalikes[x] reads as x, so a Cyrillic word's о takes a Latin o), as a substring where substring is true (Chinese, Japanese, Korean), else whole (no character of General_Category L* or N* right before or after it); a word ending in '*' is a stem: no letter or digit right before it, any letters after (Russian's case forms). In a name, every word, folded the same way. In a description, a word whose description is 'folded' the same way; 'accented' read with accents kept (NFKC, lowercase, ignorables and Me gone, on both the text and the word; French 'vérifié', whose folded form is also 'vérifie', checks); 'never' not at all (it's also an ordinary word there). In a name, a word of description.ambiguous is refused too when, read as a description is (description.about), rule 4, 2 or 'alone' says it ('已认证插件', '公式 Git 拡張', '인증됨'); and a with_kana word when it is the only CJK in the name ('公式Git'). A word with with_kana is refused only in a text that also holds kana (U+3040–30FF, U+31F0–31FF, U+FF66–FF9F): Japanese 公式 is official, Chinese 公式 a formula. The listing cases named 'the mark:' hold both sides to it.

description.about: In a description, only a glyph refuses anywhere; a mark word only when said of the plugin itself (crates/engine/src/plugins/mark.rs, Reading::said_of, is the reference). Read the folded text (and its spaced runs read as words) as words: each run of characters that aren't separators is a word, but each Han ideograph (U+3400–4DBF, U+4E00–9FFF, U+F900–FAFF, U+20000–3134F) is a word by itself. A sentence is bounded by sentence_ends. Candidates and their kind: MARK: words spelled as mark_claims reads them; languages words whose description is 'folded'; 'accented' ones in the text read with accents kept; a with_kana word that is the only CJK in the text (no other Han, kana or Hangul). NAME-ONLY: languages words whose description is 'never' and that have neither with_kana nor before. AMBIGUOUS: ambiguous, and the languages words with with_kana or before, as substrings. For each occurrence (covering the words it overlaps), in order: (4) refused when the words directly before it, or directly after it, read as one of store_words; else (negation) not refused when a word of negations is among the four words before it in its sentence, or ends the characters before it inside its word, or one of negations_after is after it in its sentence; else (object) unless a word directly before it holds a plugin_words entry ('Cliente oficial para Git'), not refused when the word directly after it in its sentence is one of object_words; else (by) when that word is one of by_words: refused when the next word after it (articles skipped) is one of authorities, else not; else (alone) refused when every word of its sentence is one it covers. Then by kind. MARK is refused when: it ends its sentence and directly before it is one of conjunctions, subject_words or predicate_before, or one of list_marks ends the characters before it in its sentence (spaces aside); or (first) for a mark word not matched as a substring, every word before it in the text is one of articles or holds no letter or digit; or (3) the word directly before it is one of subject_words; or (2, near) below. NAME-ONLY is refused when: the word directly before it is one of subject_words; or (first, as above) and the word after it is one of conjunctions; or it ends its sentence and the word before it is one of conjunctions or holds a plugin_words entry. AMBIGUOUS is refused when it ends its sentence after one of list_marks or conjunctions, or (2, near). (2, near): a plugin_words entry (whole words in order, a last word ending in '*' a stem; or a substring where substring), or for a MARK one of certified_words as a substring, with nothing in sentence_ends between, either after it with at most two words between and none of them one of relation_words nor any of relation_after among the characters between, or directly before it with no word between, or overlapping it; and the phrase not someone else's thing: walking back from the phrase's first word (skipping at most two articles), no word of relation_words; no relation_before_zh ending the characters before it (separators aside); no relation_after beginning the characters after the plugin word (separators aside). Words and phrases of these lists are compared in the reading's own form (folded, or with accents kept). The listing cases named 'description:', 'corpus:' and 'corpus3:' hold both sides to it.
description.template_about: A template's name and description are read with template_words as plugin_words too (beside them, wherever the rules above say plugin_words); a plugin's with plugin_words alone.

name beside kana; a description near a word for the plugin
name before a word for the plugin; a description near one
name before a word for the plugin; a description near one

newer_rule: A store version is newer by SemVer 2.0.0 precedence, build metadata ignored: equal precedence is the same version. A publish must be later than every version the plugin has had, in any state, pre-releases included.
template_readme_stub: This README isn't part of the interface.
templates_about: A template (contract 'Templates in the store') is a .zeron-template package (template_format), signed in template_payload_prefix's domain, or unsigned from the store under a record naming no signer, as a plugin is. Its content hash (a record's hash) is the plugin's, over its manifest without the signature and every file the package carries. template_protected: what no template replaces, each one a file or, ending '/', a folder; a path is compared after plugin-guard's fold (path.rs `fold`: '\' as '/', each character's uppercase then its lowercase, empty and '.' parts dropped, each part without its trailing dots and spaces, none of file_names.selectors in it), as the entry is, and is protected when it is one or is under one. A device leaves those files out when it installs; the store refuses a package carrying one (protected_file, field files, its path). template_listing_files: carried and installed, never part of its interface; of screenshots/, the files whose extension (ASCII case aside) is one of limits.screenshot_types, and any other file under it (its path folded as for template_protected) is refused (bad_listing, field files, its path), left out by a device and never composed; and one of them, listed in the manifest or not, whose first bytes aren't a PNG's or a JPEG's is refused too (bad_listing, field files, its path). template_manifest_fields.required must be there; allowed may be, by the plugin's rules for each; a member of template_refused_members may not (bad_listing, that field, in that list's order); nor may any other but signature (bad_listing, field manifest, word the member, in code point order). template_readme_stub: a README.md holding it is the one Zeron wrote (missing_readme). preview.png must be a still PNG (no acTL chunk, read chunk by chunk from the signature while a whole chunk header remains) of at most limits.max_preview_bytes (bad_listing, field preview; missing_listing when there's none); screenshots are under screenshots/. A template's engines_zeron is '>=' + its zeron_version. The template_listing and template_packages cases hold both sides to it.
unseen: A name or description may hold no character drawn as nothing (bad_listing): a control or format character (General_Category Cc, Cf), any other Default_Ignorable_Code_Point (the Hangul fillers among them), any Variation_Selector but U+FE0F, and U+FE0F only directly after a character with the Emoji property. Keywords are ASCII. The listing cases named 'unseen:' hold both sides to it.
